newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Leading journalists on the Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDA) are planning a big push for greater freedom of information and measures to prevent media monopolies by either the government or the private sector. A freedom of information bill was neutralised in the latest House dissolution. Critics, however, say the bill will have been of little help as far as press freedom is concerned, even if it had been passed. (THE NATION)

- A proposal to combat drugs with an all-powerful panel with authority to conduct searches without warrants has been rejected by Interior Minister Sanoh Thienthong. He says the Interior Ministry is in charge of drugs prevention and suppression, and any such outfit would cause a duplication of work. (BANGKOK POST)

- Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung, who has been actively combatting the use and sale of drugs in nightspots, plans to increase the scope of his operation to include shutting down places which serve underage customers and violate closing times. He says any establishment found serving customers under 18 years of age faces immediate closure and frequent offenders could have their licences revoked temporarily. (THE NATION)

- Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance Chatumongkol Sonakul has denied an accusation of malfeasance in approving the cancellation of a bad debt of more tahn 110 million baht in favour of Sinsub Siam Company. The allegation was made following the recent reshuffle of senior finance ministry officials organised by Chatumongkol. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Fixed and cellular telephone services will be the first of the liberalised sectors not to be subject to royalty fees, but will have to compete on the basis of consumer benefits, says Transport and Communications Minister Suwat Liptapanlop. The liberalisation plan will be implemented with a new bidding system under which licences will be issued to investors to replace the current system of awarding concession contracts. (THE NATION)
